caption: The TNT duper (vjeux 2026-10-20: one world-best implementation, built from catalog parts): 86 lit TNT a minute, standing right on the ground. Two catalog parts. The 16-block duplicator engine (tnt-triggered-launch-16b's, without its input block) makes one TNT each time its sticky piston loses power for a moment: held extended, released, it retracts, the redstone block on its slime frame comes back next to its dust and pushes it out again, which primes a TNT and throws it north at 1 block per tick. The clock is clk-obs-p14-lamp-obs-rb-stk-6b-b-0e0eb7 from the clock catalog (6 blocks, period 14 gt): its sticky piston moves a redstone block that sits next to the engine's piston (holding it) except for 4 ticks of every 14, so the engine dupes once per period. Each TNT lands and explodes on the ground 9 to 30 blocks away (7.4 to 27 on unbreakable ground), beyond the 6.9 blocks a blast can reach, so no explosion touches the machine and each one breaks ground blocks. Found by `mctas circuit tnt hold-scan` (every archived clock and turn, the cells where a piston is powered on all but one short window of the period, the engine's piston put there, judged on redsim); the 120-TNT-a-minute version (a period-10 clock) lands blasts as close as 5.3 blocks and failed 1 of 16 game builds in 3 of 6 runs. material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 1 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 2 -1 2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there)

Precise air burst, 44 blocks in a 5x5x10 box (250), 22.2 TNT/min: every lit TNT explodes at exactly the same point in the air, bit for bit, safe on the ground. clk-rt's minimum-volume search (explore/timer 37ee0ae37, designs/circuits/tracks/clk-rt/tnt-airburst-250-44b.txt): the 45-block 250-volume version with one block fewer. The 16b engine is held by a redstone torch that a 7-block catalog P54 clock darkens for one TNT per period; the TNT flies into fence posts over a water channel, the current pins it against a fence post standing on a slime block, and the next TNT's push, carried by observers, makes the sticky piston under the slime launch it straight up, so it explodes near the top of its flight, more than 7 blocks from anything a blast could break. material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 2 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 5 1 -2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there); obsidian at 6 0 -7 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there)

One TNT per BUTTON press (site QA 2026-10-21: a real button holds 20-30 gt, so the 16-block engine judged with a 4-tick removal of its holding redstone block lit several TNT per press). The engine of tnt-triggered-launch-16b with a one-shot hold instead: the obsidian beside the piston is strongly powered by a wall torch under it, which holds the piston; the torch hangs on the stone under the piston (in the obsidian foot's place) and the button is on that stone. A press powers the stone: the stone holds the piston itself and the torch goes dark. At the release the stone goes quiet 2 ticks before the torch relights: the piston drops, the frame comes back, its redstone block repowers the piston through the dust and the push lights ONE TNT, however long the press. Latency: the press, then 5 ticks.

The clockless TNT engine with an on/off LEVER (vjeux 2026-10-21: "I thought we were going to remove the clock as we didn't need it"; "Can we have an on off switch for all the tnt"): tnt-triggered-launch-16b's engine, its holding redstone block replaced by a torch that holds the engine piston (lit while the lever is off) and the lever on the torch's stone; the obsidian under the piston is not needed. Lever off (as built): the torch holds the sticky piston extended, nothing moves. Lever on: the torch goes dark and the engine runs by itself, its frame's redstone block re-powering the piston through the dust every cycle: one TNT per 6 gt (200 TNT/min). Lever off again: the torch relights within 2 gt and the piston stays extended. It stands 6 blocks above the ground (stand: its safe drop over every kick: the TNT bursts under it).

Precise drop, 41 blocks in a 6x5x8 box (240), 30 TNT/min: every TNT falls straight down from one point and explodes at one point in mid-air 10.0 blocks under the machine, 13.0 blocks above the ground it stands 23 blocks over. clk-rt's minimum-volume search (explore/timer 3670274e4, designs/circuits/tracks/clk-rt/tnt-precise-drop-240-41b.txt): the 240-volume version with 3 fewer blocks. A 7-block catalog P40 clock, folded between the engine and the channel, moves its redstone block in front of a repeater for 6 ticks every 40 and the torch under the engine piston goes dark: one TNT. The TNT flies into fence posts over a water channel, the current pins it against an observer on an iron trapdoor, and the next TNT's push, carried by observers and a delay-4 repeater, opens the trapdoor. material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 1 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 5 -2 2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there) 2026-10-21: 2 blocks stored as a player's placement shapes them (`mctas clock shapes`: a fence's arms, a gate's in_wall, a tripwire's connections)

Precise drop with an on/off lever, ONE clock + ONE item-free delay (coordinator 2026-10-21 after vjeux 15:24Z: no exposed hoppers; "it's just one clock + delay circuit"): tnt-precise-drop (41b) with the 52b's lever inverter holding its clock, and its release chain made long enough that each TNT is released by its OWN push: the observer watching the engine's frame starts a line of six delay-4 repeaters (48 gt) to the repeater the trapdoor's observer watches. A stop never strands a TNT: the last push's delayed release still comes. Not compacted yet (clk-rt's compact).

Precise air burst with an on/off lever, ONE clock + ONE item-free delay (coordinator 2026-10-21 after vjeux 15:24Z: no exposed hoppers; "it's just one clock + delay circuit"): tnt-airburst-lever-56b with its hopper ring, dropper and comparator replaced by a repeater line: the 44b's observer watching the frame's redstone block powers a stone over a dust at y = 1, then 62 gt of repeaters around x = 8..9 and down x = 7 at y = 0 (out of reach of the bursts above) end in a repeater whose observer pulses the launcher's obsidian, so each TNT is launched by its OWN push and a stop never strands one. The lever's torch holds the clock's downward piston; the file draws the machine as the lever leaves it. Not compacted yet (clk-rt's compact). material (clk-rt 2026-10-21, `circuit material`): 2 obsidian -> stone (the same kind, axis and metrics on its judge); obsidian at 5 1 -2 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there); obsidian at 6 0 -7 stays for immovability (pistons must not move it: the design fails or changes even with a blast-proof netherite block there)

The fast TNT engine with its lever's inverter moved off the bottom (coordinator 2026-10-21, after vjeux 15:17Z "is 6 blocks the safe minimum?"; the site ranks TNT dupers by effective volume = the box + the air it needs under it): tnt-engine-lever-17b's engine (200 TNT/min) with the torch on the side of a stone behind the engine's piston and the lever on top of that stone, instead of a torch and a wall lever under the machine. 3x3x5 instead of 4x4x4: 15 x (3 + 7) = 150 vs 16 x (4 + 6) = 160. The safe drop (7) is still set by the engine's own un-launched TNT (per-spawn run 58: TNT 7, kick 0.087751, stays on the ground under the machine and breaks a moving piston block first).
